claims.text: Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 is a high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a heterogeneous dendritic/interdendritic microstructure.
The as-cast alloy has spatially variable local chemical disorder.
Homogenization and annealing can convert the as-cast microstructure toward a more uniform gamma-phase-based matrix.
The heat-treated state is a uniform gamma-phase matrix.
The proposed heat treatments can tune disorder while leaving phase composition unchanged.
High configurational entropy in HEAs is associated with substantial chemical disorder on a crystalline lattice.
Homogenizing this alloy enhances electron-phonon coupling in the dirty limit.
An optimal intermediate level of local disorder maximizes electron-phonon coupling, whereas either excess or paucity of disorder weakens it.
Homogenization-induced electron-phonon coupling will produce coherent isotropic s-wave BCS pairing in Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6.
Some superconducting HEAs are dirty-limit, single-band, isotropic s-wave superconductors consistent with a BCS description.
The heat-treated Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 alloy will become superconducting at approximately 7–10 K.
Homogenized samples will show a sharp transition to zero electrical resistance and a well-defined Meissner effect.
Systematic tuning of chemical homogeneity will cause corresponding changes in Tc and the critical fields.
As-cast heterogeneous samples will have broadened or suppressed superconducting transitions relative to homogenized samples.
Rapid quenching creates excessive disorder that lies outside the proposed enhancement regime.
Extensive heat treatment can cause phase evolution in this alloy.
Competing phase transformations may affect the superconducting properties of this alloy.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes samples that undergo unintended phase transformations from the hypothesis's valid regime, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of such transformations and associated anomalous superconductivity as falsification rather than as an out-of-domain result.
